name: Schönwies
kurzbeschreibung: Lively community in the Oberinntal with excellent transport links and idyllic nature along the Inn river.
beschreibung:
Overview

Schönwies lies at an altitude of 737 meters in the Tyrolean Oberinntal valley, nestled between Imst downstream and the Landeck-Zams basin upstream. Home to approximately 1,800 residents, the municipality comprises 14 traditional hamlets, including Schönwies-Dorf, Starkenbach, Obsaurs, Ried, and Saurs. The landscape extends from the sunny valley floor along the Inn river up into the slopes of the Lechtal Alps and the Venet range. Defined by the prominent rocky bluff of Kronburg, Schönwies preserves a quiet, rural atmosphere blending outdoor sports, climbing, cultural pilgrimage, and family hiking trails away from mass tourism.

History

Human settlement dates back to antiquity, as the Roman Via Claudia Augusta crossed the valley floor. In the 19th century, a hoard of Roman silver coins was unearthed in Starkenbach. The village was first documented in 1290 as Schönwiz. Around 1380, Hans von Starkenberg built Kronburg Castle atop a rocky vantage point. Following feudal conflicts, Duke Friedrich IV acquired the stronghold in 1423, which was later granted to the Lords of Fieger by Emperor Maximilian I. The baroque pilgrimage church of Maria Hilf Kronburg originated from a miraculous recovery in 1673 and was erected between 1714 and 1717 next to the Klause hermitage. The parish church of Saint Michael was built between 1681 and 1686.

Getting there

Schönwies is conveniently accessible by road and rail. By car, take the Inntal motorway A12 to Imst or the S16 Arlberg expressway to Zams, continuing along federal road B171 directly into the village. Train passengers arrive via Schönwies railway station on the Arlberg railway, served hourly by S-Bahn trains connecting directly to Landeck-Zams, Imst-Pitztal, and Innsbruck. Regional VVT buses connect the outer hamlets with the village core and the hiking trailheads.

Tips

Visit the hilltop ruins of Kronburg Castle at 1,066 meters for panoramic valley vistas and traditional Tyrolean cuisine at the Klause Kronburg guesthouse. Explore the rugged Kronburg gorge with its cascading torrents, or enjoy sport climbing at the south-facing Starkenbach crag, part of the Climbers Paradise network. Cyclists can pedal along the Inn Cycle Path, while walkers can follow the Way of Saint James up to the pilgrimage sanctuary.
